headline: North Korea Fires Multiple Missiles Toward the East Sea
deck: Seoul's Joint Chiefs detected the Pyongyang-area launches at about 9:20 a.m.; Japan counted two, the longer flying more than 910 km into the Sea of Japan.

flashpoint.note: JCS timed Pyongyang-area launches at about 9:20 a.m. Japan counted two; types remain unpublished.

body: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Monday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. [E1][E2][E3]
The Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the launches from the Pyongyang area at about 9:20 a.m. and that at least one of the missiles flew more than 900 kilometers. [E4][E5]
Japan's Defense Ministry said it had detected two separate launches. [E6]
The first missile, fired at around 9:19 a.m., traveled about 220 km and reached a maximum altitude of 20 km, the ministry said. [E7]
The second, launched around 9:36 a.m., flew more than 910 km, at a maximum altitude of 70 km. [E8]
Both splashed down in the Sea of Japan, outside Japan's exclusive economic zone. [E9]

Monday's launch marked North Korea's 16th round of ballistic missile launches this year, following its previous launch on Oct. 3. [E10] Monday's Pyongyang-area rounds are a later event than this paper's August East Sea salvo during Ulchi Freedom Shield and September's Wonsan launches.
